title: Billo vs AI UGC Ads: Real Creators or AI Presenters Compared
summary: Billo vs AI UGC ads compared on real creators, partnership ads, published prices and disclosure duties, so you can pick the right format for your brief.
body_markdown:
## How do those prices compare with the creator market?


Billo's $99 starting price sits close to what brands advertise for UGC. The Pitchlo UGC Pay Report counts 645 per-video briefs posted between December 2025 and October 2026, with a median offer of $100 per video and half between $50 and $200. Those are advertised budgets, not settled invoices ([Pitchlo UGC Pay Report](https://www.pitchlo.com/ugc-creator-earnings) ).


Collabstr's 2026 report puts the average UGC asking price at $180 and the average paid price at $154 per engagement, from 2025 marketplace data ([Collabstr 2026 report](https://collabstr.com/2026-influencer-marketing-report) ). Usage rights move the number: Collabstr's 2025 report found influencer campaigns with usage rights averaged $307, against $221 without, across all campaign types and not only UGC ([Collabstr 2025 report](https://collabstr.com/2025-influencer-marketing-report) ). Billo includes usage rights in its $99, so check what "usage rights" covers, such as channels and duration, before you compare it with a quote that adds them as a line item.


## Which other AI UGC providers sit beside Knowlify?


**Unreal UGC** makes AI UGC with AI creators only, sells white-label service to agencies, and lists 5 to 500 ads a month with a 3 to 5 day turnaround. Done-for-you pricing is not published ([Unreal UGC](https://unrealugc.com/agency) ).


**Creatify Studio** is managed AI video production with a creative team. Its pricing page lists 25 to 100+ videos a month with a 48-hour turnaround. Its comparison table puts Studio at $100 to $200 per video, so ask whether it includes any campaign work ([Creatify Studio](https://creatify.ai/studio) ).


**EditClub** makes AI UGC-style actors and product shots with no creators, for DTC brands spending $10,000 or more a month on Meta. Its Crew plan costs $1,600 a month for about 60 videos with 72-hour delivery, and its Club and Partner plans deliver in 24 to 48 hours ([EditClub](https://www.editclub.co/) ).


## Where AI UGC meets disclosure rules


Two sets of rules matter for AI UGC: Meta's labels and the FTC's testimonial guidance. Meta labels ads with photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own generative AI creative tools, and the label sits next to the Sponsored label. Meta also says it will detect ads made or edited with third-party AI tools and show an AI info label. Its post does not say that detection is live yet ([Meta's AI transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) ).


The FTC's testimonial Q&A does not impose a blanket ban on AI avatars, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false ([FTC testimonial Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) ). Script an AI presenter in your brand's voice, not as a customer. For the wider cost picture, see[AI UGC vs creator UGC cost](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-ugc-vs-creator-ugc-cost) .


Real creators bring their own rules. For partnership ads, the creator must grant permission, or Meta holds the ad in a pending state ([Meta partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/ad-creative/partnership-ads/ads-creation) ).


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for AI UGC ads, with about 25 finished ads a week and a first batch on day 5.
- Billo fits when a real creator's account, face or words matter, including partnership ads from creator handles.
- Billo publishes videos from $99 each and a managed service from $2,000 a month, but no turnaround.
- AI presenters cannot run partnership ads or deliver a real customer's testimonial.
- Compare both on one written brief, with revisions, usage rights and disclosure duties priced in.


## FAQ


### Which is best for UGC ads, Billo or AI UGC?


Knowlify is our top pick for AI UGC ads when your brief does not need a real person. Billo is the better choice when a creator's account or a real customer's experience matters. Price both on the same brief, with revisions and usage rights included.


### Which is cheaper, Billo or AI UGC?


Billo lists videos from $99 each, and its managed service starts at $2,000 a month. Knowlify starts at $5,000 a month, and Creatify Studio's comparison table lists $100 to $200 per video. Compare total cost, including complexity bonuses and revisions, rather than the headline price.


### Can an AI presenter run partnership ads?


No. Meta's partnership ads run from a creator's or partner's handle, and an AI presenter generated for your ads has no handle of its own. Use a real creator when the ad must run from a person's account.


### Does AI UGC need a label on Meta?


Meta labels photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own tools, and says it will detect third-party AI tools and show an AI info label. Its post does not say that detection is live yet, so plan for disclosure in your approvals.


### Does one format convert better?


Our sources do not compare the results of these two formats, and we did not test either one. Test both on the same offer and audience, and judge them on approved, delivered ads and cost per result.
